About me

The road SO FAR

I don't have an overnight success story. I have a long sequence of small decisions, almost all of them made with incomplete information.

The beginning

I started working early, in jobs where nobody asked my opinion. So I learned to watch. I quickly noticed that almost every problem that looked technical was really an unresolved communication problem.

The first time I led a team I was in my early twenties with no management training. I got plenty wrong: I wanted to be liked, I avoided difficult conversations, I assumed people could guess what I expected of them. It was the best school I could have had.

Building

Today I run projects in education and adult training. I work with small teams, where there's nowhere to hide poor organisation, and with clients who trust us with time they can't get back.

My days sit between operational decisions and decisions about direction. Hiring, programmes, rooms, budgets. I like the detail: the temperature of a room and the tone of an email say as much about an organisation as its strategic plan.

On stage

I've been speaking publicly since I realised that what I learned the hard way could save someone else time. I talk about everyday leadership, about building teams with limited resources, and about what nobody tells you about growing.

I prepare each talk from scratch, for the context of whoever invites me. I don't bring a generic deck and I don't use the stage to sell anything.

Outside all this

I live in Portugal, I read more than I can keep up with, and I still think the best idea in any meeting tends to show up in the last five minutes.

If you've read this far, we probably have something to talk about. My inbox is open.
